comparisons.peer_topic: Adoption of ASU No. 2023-02 for Tax Credit Structures
comparisons.peer_summary: Citi adopted ASU No. 2023-02 effective January 1, 2024, allowing the use of the proportional amortization method for certain tax-incentivized investments, which had no material impact on the financial statements.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and Citi adopted ASU 2023-02 effective January 1, 2024, which allows for the proportional amortization method for tax credit investments, resulting in the classification of amortization and tax credits within income tax expense. JPM reported a $161 million decrease to retained earnings and a $450 million increase in income tax expense, noting no material impact to net income. In contrast, Citi also adopted the standard on January 1, 2024, but reported no material impact to its financial statements.

sentences.text: The adoption of this guidance resulted in a change to the classification and timing of the amortization associated with certain of the Firm's alternative energy tax-oriented investments.

The change in accounting resulted in a decrease to retained earnings of $161 million and increased the Firm's income tax expense and the effective tax rate by approximately $450 million and two percentage points, respectively, in the first quarter of 2024, with no material impact to net income.
As a result of the adoption, the amortization of these investments that was previously recognized in other income is now recognized in income tax expense.

Under the proportional amortization method, the cost of an eligible investment is amortized in proportion to the income tax credits and other income tax benefits that are received by the investor, with the amortization of the investment and the income tax credits being presented net in the income statement as components of income tax expense (benefit).
Citi adopted the ASU on January 1, 2024, which did not have a material impact to the financial statements of the Company.

comparisons.comparison: Goldman Sachs and JPM both disclose financial data related to investments in qualified affordable housing and renewable energy projects that meet the criteria for the proportional amortization method. JPM explicitly states that the adoption of the guidance resulted in classifying amortization for these alternative energy tax-oriented investments into income tax expense. Goldman Sachs provides a table presenting information regarding the amortization and related income tax credits and benefits for similar projects under the proportional amortization method.

comparisons.peer_topic: Financial Impact of Tax Credit Accounting Update Adoption
comparisons.peer_summary: The adoption of the accounting update resulted in a $60 million net-of-tax decrease to Retained earnings and a corresponding reduction to Other assets as of January 1, 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and Morgan Stanley adopted the accounting update for tax credit structures effective January 1, 2024, using the modified retrospective method. Both disclosures highlight a decrease to retained earnings as a direct financial impact of this adoption. JPM reported a $161 million decrease to retained earnings, while Morgan Stanley reported a $60 million net-of-tax decrease to retained earnings. Both firms reclassified amortization and tax benefits to income tax expense.
